{
  "summary": "Adds a `-reobfuscate-blocks[=<value>]` startup option to rewrite existing `blk*.dat` and `rev*.dat` files under a newly generated or user-specified XOR key before chainstate loading. File migrations are processed single-threaded in chunks, staged with temporary suffixes and fsync commits to ensure crash safety and resumability across restarts. Also logs an informational recommendation to reobfuscate when an unobfuscated blocks directory is detected, and exposes progress through kernel notifications for the GUI.",
  "problem": "Nodes synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 store block and undo files with an all-zero XOR key (unobfuscated), leaving them susceptible to antivirus scanners misidentifying block payloads and quarantining or corrupting files. Node operators currently have no native way to obfuscate existing files, rotate keys, or remove obfuscation without redownloading the entire chain.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description explains that \"Nodes that synced before v28 may store block and undo files effectively unobfuscated with a zero XOR key. There is no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate their key, or deliberately replace it with a zero key without resyncing.\"",
    "External demand is corroborated by prior efforts to address this issue via standalone tooling (PR #32451 and external tool `andrewtoth/blocks-xor`).",
    "Author provides migration benchmarks across 5 hardware configurations ranging from ~10 minutes for 854 GB on an Apple M4 Max SSD to ~24.5 hours on a Raspberry Pi 4B HDD."
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "Modifies node startup initialization and block storage file management. It also updates `DirectoryCommit` to return a boolean error status and cleans up an unused obfuscation parameter in `BaseIndex::DB`.",
  "changed_since_previous": "Added an informational log suggestion prompting users to reobfuscate when blocksdir XOR is inactive, made `DirectoryCommit` return a boolean status with unit test coverage, and removed an unused obfuscation parameter from `BaseIndex::DB`.",
  "card": "Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option to rewrite existing block and undo files under a random or user-specified XOR key. Datadirs synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 remain unobfuscated, leaving node storage vulnerable to false-positive file corruption by antivirus software unless the user resyncs the chain from scratch. The migration is crash-safe, resumable if interrupted, and reports progress to GUI and logs. No dependencies are noted.",
  "needs": [],
  "confidence": "high",
  "uncertainties": [],
  "risk": {
    "level": "medium",
    "touches": ["validation", "gui", "other"],
    "why": "A failure or flaw in staging, committing, or renaming files during block rewriting could corrupt or destroy blk/rev files, requiring the operator to re-download the chain."
  }
}

result.summary: Adds a `-reobfuscate-blocks[=<value>]` startup option to rewrite existing `blk*.dat` and `rev*.dat` files under a newly generated or user-specified XOR key before chainstate loading. File migrations are processed single-threaded in chunks, staged with temporary suffixes and fsync commits to ensure crash safety and resumability across restarts. Also logs an informational recommendation to reobfuscate when an unobfuscated blocks directory is detected, and exposes progress through kernel notifications for the GUI.
result.problem: Nodes synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 store block and undo files with an all-zero XOR key (unobfuscated), leaving them susceptible to antivirus scanners misidentifying block payloads and quarantining or corrupting files. Node operators currently have no native way to obfuscate existing files, rotate keys, or remove obfuscation without redownloading the entire chain.
evidence: PR description explains that "Nodes that synced before v28 may store block and undo files effectively unobfuscated with a zero XOR key. There is no built-in way to obfuscate those existing files, rotate their key, or deliberately replace it with a zero key without resyncing."
External demand is corroborated by prior efforts to address this issue via standalone tooling (PR #32451 and external tool `andrewtoth/blocks-xor`).
Author provides migration benchmarks across 5 hardware configurations ranging from ~10 minutes for 854 GB on an Apple M4 Max SSD to ~24.5 hours on a Raspberry Pi 4B HDD.
result.scope_notes: Modifies node startup initialization and block storage file management. It also updates `DirectoryCommit` to return a boolean error status and cleans up an unused obfuscation parameter in `BaseIndex::DB`.
result.changed_since_previous: Added an informational log suggestion prompting users to reobfuscate when blocksdir XOR is inactive, made `DirectoryCommit` return a boolean status with unit test coverage, and removed an unused obfuscation parameter from `BaseIndex::DB`.
result.card: Adds a -reobfuscate-blocks startup option to rewrite existing block and undo files under a random or user-specified XOR key. Datadirs synced prior to Bitcoin Core v28 remain unobfuscated, leaving node storage vulnerable to false-positive file corruption by antivirus software unless the user resyncs the chain from scratch. The migration is crash-safe, resumable if interrupted, and reports progress to GUI and logs. No dependencies are noted.

risk.why: A failure or flaw in staging, committing, or renaming files during block rewriting could corrupt or destroy blk/rev files, requiring the operator to re-download the chain.
